Emily —

Appreciate the clear list. Below is a concise proposal we can put into the security exhibit redline so you and your team have something concrete to review: (I’ve also attached a redline draft and a simple evidence manifest template.)

High level proposal (summary to be inserted into security exhibit / order form appendix):
1) Pen-test notice & windows:
   - Mutual 30-day standard notice for planned penetration testing.
   - Up to two (2) five-calendar-day active test windows per rolling 12 months; additional windows by mutual agreement.
   - No-tests blackout: 72-hour blackout for major releases unless both parties opt in via documented change control.

2) Staging & access:
   - Testing limited to customer-provisioned staging or pre-prod environments; production testing only with explicit written approval and an agreed scope.
   - Ephemeral credentials (time-limited JWTs or short-lived API keys) and read-only accounts for evidence collection.

3) SOC 2 artifacts & lookback:
   - Redwood will provide SOC 2 Type II report (most recent 12-month period) where available. If report is in process, provide a bridge letter and SOC audit contact.

4) Evidence cadence & delivery:
   - Weekly evidence snapshot cadence during a scheduled evidence sprint (CSV manifest + logs bundle if requested).
   - Evidence types: auth logs, API access logs, deployment configs, infra inventory, and architectural diagrams (as applicable).
   - Retention: operational evidence will be available for 90 days from collection for review; audit artifacts (SOC reports) retained per contractual retention schedule.

5) Scope & limitations:
   - Pen-test scope to be agreed in advance; tests must exclude customer PII exfiltration and must follow mutually agreed disclosure rules.
   - All findings reported to named points-of-contact and submitted to our tracker (we’ll provide an internal JIRA ticket).

6) Confidentiality & reporting:
   - All test findings shared under existing NDA; Redwood will not publish or share findings outside the agreed remediation channel.

Next steps I propose: legal review of the redline we’ve attached, then a 30-minute kickoff call to agree the initial inspection matrix and pick dates for a staging test window. Proposed slots: Fri 20 Nov 14:00–15:00 PT or Mon 23 Nov 09:00–10:00 PT.

Attachments: RNK_MSA_SecurityExhibit_REDLINE.docx; evidence_manifest_template.csv

If you’re ok, I’ll loop in Laura for the final redline language and Priyom for operational handoff.

—Karthik

Karthik / Priyom —

Thanks for drafting. A few legal points to tighten before we send the formal redline to HealthNet procurement:

- Limit inspections to two (2) 5-day windows per rolling 12 months (as proposed) but add language allowing additional windows for regulatory or incident response, with a written escalation path and cost allocation if extra windows are requested by the customer.
- Add a clause that pen-tests require a scoped statement of work (SOW) and an explicit list of approved IP ranges and accounts; otherwise tests are limited to sandbox/staging.
- Require that penetration testers sign Redwood’s standard contractor NDA and provide proof of professional liability insurance (minimum $1M).
- For SOC 2, change wording to: "Redwood will provide the most recent SOC 2 Type II report where available; if not available, Redwood will provide a SOC 2 bridge letter and auditor contact within 14 days of request." This avoids committing to delivery when report cycles shift.
- Evidence retention: preserve original logs for at least 120 days internally; make exportable snapshots available to the customer for 90 days per the proposed cadence.
- Add a non-destructive testing requirement and explicit prohibition on exploit chaining that could cause data loss; allow the customer to request an emergency pause with 2-hour response SLA from Redwood.

If HealthNet accepts these constraints we should be able to close the security exhibit quickly. I’ll draft the specific clause language into the attached redline. Priyom — please confirm operations can meet the 120-day internal retention and the 2-hour emergency pause SLA.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Security
Redwood Inference
